failed_calls_retries.assessment: The session had substantial early tool-surface friction: seven rejected apply_ops calls, including three consecutive attempts to invent the addSection geometry schema. One additional call applied successfully but its automatic render failed because the sections omitted required text. The agent recovered without a session retry, but the repeated schema guessing constitutes one parse/validation fight.

lint_etiquette.assessment: Lint handling was disciplined once lint appeared. Twelve initial errors and numerous warnings were reduced aggressively; a later containment error was also fixed on the next turn. There was no repeated firing of the same lint for more than three consecutive turns without a strategy change. The sole committed warning was explicitly identified and reasoned in the commit summary rather than silently overridden.

commit_honesty.assessment: The single commit summary accurately describes the added three-stage incident-response workflow and explicitly discloses the one remaining warning. The stage diff contains the claimed escalation, mitigation verification/retry, resolution, and follow-up structures. The disclosed border issue matches the final W1 lint. No inflated claim or undeclared defect demonstrably seen by the agent was found.

economy.assessment: The session completed well within budget at about 5.84 minutes, but it was not mechanically economical. Early schema guessing caused rejected batches, and the malformed sections were removed and re-added in a clear add-delete-rebuild cycle. Later operations were generally purposeful, especially the large lint-reduction round, and the final committed diff was 47 patch operations.
